hints: Override the draw method in OutlineRect to render both fill and stroke
Draw the fill first, then the stroke on top
exercises.explanation: OutlineRect overrides draw() to render both fill and stroke. The child defines its own version of the method, which takes precedence over the parent's.

exercises.title: Encapsulated State Machine
hints: Return an object with functions that close over the private state
The transition function should check if the target state is in the allowed list for the current state
exercises.explanation: The state machine only allows valid transitions. idle->walking->running works, but running->jumping fails because that transition isn't defined. The final state remains 'running'.

exercises.title: Encapsulated Animation Controller
hints: Implement the step function with spring physics: displacement = target - position
Apply damping to velocity and update position
exercises.explanation: The spring controller uses encapsulated physics state. After one second, the spring settles at its target position because velocity approaches zero and displacement is within the threshold.

exercises.title: Weak Privacy with Conventions
hints: Use underscore prefix (_) for fields and methods that should be considered private
Implement the public setColor method to update _paint.color
exercises.explanation: Underscore conventions indicate 'private' fields that shouldn't be accessed directly from outside the class. The _dirty flag is set to true initially, then false after _rebuildPath runs.

exercises.title: Module Pattern
hints: The emit function should call createParticle (private helper) and add to the particles array
The update function should filter out dead particles (life <= 0)
exercises.explanation: The module pattern combines closures with a clean factory interface. Private helpers (createParticle, updateParticle) are completely hidden. After emitting 5 particles, the count is 5.

exercises.title: Read-Only Properties
hints: Getters simply return the private variables
addScore should add points and check for level up (level = floor(score/1000) + 1)
exercises.explanation: Read-only properties can only be modified through validated setter methods. Direct assignment fails because the field doesn't exist on the returned object - only the getter function exists.

exercises.title: Combining Approaches
hints: The Timer module uses closures for true privacy
The Countdown class uses underscore conventions for internal details
exercises.explanation: Real applications combine both approaches: closures for critical state (timer logic) and conventions for internal implementation details (UI paths/paints). This gives you security where it matters and simplicity where it doesn't.

exercises.title: Factory Pattern
hints: Check config.type and return the appropriate shape
Use if/elseif to handle each type
exercises.explanation: The factory centralizes object creation. With 3 configs (circle, rectangle, triangle), the factory creates 3 shapes. Adding new shape types only requires modifying the factory, not client code.

exercises.title: Prototype Pattern (Clone)
hints: The clone method creates a new object with setmetatable
Copy all fields and clone the path
exercises.explanation: The Prototype pattern avoids expensive initialization. Templates are created once (expensive), then spawned many times via cheap cloning.

exercises.title: Module Pattern (IIFE)
hints: Use an IIFE to create private scope
Return public interface with functions that use private helpers
exercises.explanation: The Module pattern uses IIFEs to create private scope. Private helpers and constants are hidden; only the public interface is exposed.

exercises.title: Singleton Pattern
hints: Use an IIFE with private cache table
Check if key exists before calling loader
exercises.explanation: The Singleton ensures only one cache instance exists. When requesting the same key twice, the first call is a miss, the second is a hit.

exercises.title: Observer Pattern
hints: Only notify observers if value actually changed
Store callbacks and call each with (newValue, oldValue)
exercises.explanation: The Observer pattern provides reactive updates. When a value changes, all subscribed observers are automatically notified.

exercises.title: Console Exploration

exercises.title: Type Safety with --!strict

exercises.title: Click Counter with Visual Feedback
hints: Return true to consume the event
exercises.explanation: Pointer events use boolean returns to consume or propagate events, similar to stopPropagation().

exercises.title: Drag and Drop
hints: Calculate offset in pointerDown for natural dragging
Only process move/up when isDragging is true
exercises.explanation: Drag behavior requires all three pointer events working together.

exercises.title: Input-Driven State Visualization
hints: update() is called when inputs change
exercises.explanation: Scripts respond to state machine inputs through update() callback for bidirectional data flow.

exercises.title: Publisher-Subscriber Pattern
hints: EventBus uses module-level state shared across scripts
Use table.insert for subscribe, ipairs for publish
exercises.explanation: Pub/sub pattern enables decoupled component communication via shared EventBus Util.

exercises.title: Draw a Line
hints: Use moveTo to set the start position
Use lineTo to draw to the end position
Create a stroke paint with thickness and color
exercises.explanation: moveTo sets the pen position without drawing, lineTo draws a line to the target. These are the most basic path operations.

exercises.title: Filled Rectangle with Outline
hints: Build a rectangle using moveTo, lineTo, close
Create two paints: fill and stroke
Draw fill first, then stroke on top
exercises.explanation: close() connects back to the start. Draw fill first, then stroke on top. One path can be drawn multiple times.

exercises.title: Fill vs Stroke
hints: Fill colors the interior of a closed shape
Use cap for line endings, join for corners
exercises.explanation: Fill and stroke are the two fundamental paint styles. Fill colors the interior, stroke draws the outline.

exercises.title: Gradient Fill
hints: Gradient.linear takes start point, end point, and color stops
Each stop has position (0-1) and color
Gradient overrides the solid color property
exercises.explanation: Linear gradients interpolate colors between two points. Color stops define which colors appear at which positions.

exercises.title: Paint Variations with copy()
hints: Use paint:copy({ property = value }) to create variations
The copied paint inherits all settings
Override only the properties you want to change
exercises.explanation: paint:copy() creates a new paint with inherited settings. This is more efficient than creating separate paints with redundant properties.

exercises.title: Translate and Rotate a Shape
hints: Use save() before transforms, restore() after
Increment angle in advance, apply in draw
exercises.explanation: The renderer maintains a transform stack. save() pushes state, transform() applies matrices, restore() pops state.

exercises.title: Multiple Instances with save/restore
hints: Use a for loop with save/restore inside
Each iteration applies its own transform
One path can be drawn multiple times
exercises.explanation: save/restore in a loop lets you draw the same path multiple times with independent transforms.

exercises.title: Animated Polyline
hints: Use path:reset() at start of advance
Loop through points with moveTo for first, lineTo for rest
exercises.explanation: Dynamic paths are rebuilt in advance() using reset(). Never call reset() in draw().

exercises.title: Clipping a Region
hints: Draw content, then restore() to clear clip
exercises.explanation: clipPath() restricts all subsequent drawing to inside the clip region. Cleared by restore().

exercises.title: Press to Toggle Color
hints: Use ternary pattern: cond and valueA or valueB
Call event:hit() to consume the event
exercises.explanation: pointerDown handles click events. Toggle state with 'not', update visuals, and call event:hit() to stop propagation.

exercises.title: Track Multiple Pointers
hints: Use event.id as the table key
Create entry in pointerDown, update in pointerMove
Set to nil in pointerUp to remove
exercises.explanation: Each pointer has a unique event.id. Track them in a table: create on down, update on move, remove on up.

exercises.title: Spawn Multiple Instances
hints: Store in a table with position data
Call advance() and draw() on each instance
exercises.explanation: Dynamic instantiation creates runtime copies of component artboards. You must call advance() and draw() on each instance every frame.

exercises.title: Procedural Polygon
hints: Loop from 0 to n-1 for vertices
Use cos for x, sin for y
exercises.explanation: Regular polygons are built by distributing points evenly around a circle. The angle offset (-π/2) makes the first vertex point upward.

exercises.title: Animated Star
hints: Alternate radius: outer for even, inner for odd
exercises.explanation: Stars alternate between outer and inner radius. Animating the innerRatio creates a pulsing effect.

exercises.title: Sine Wave Path
hints: Loop through segments for smooth curve
Add time to phase for animation
Use stroke style for open paths
exercises.explanation: Adding time to the sine phase creates animation. More segments means smoother curves.

exercises.title: Bezier Curves
hints: Use sine wave for flowing motion
exercises.explanation: cubicTo creates smooth curves using two control points. Animating them creates elegant flowing motion.

exercises.title: Simple Particle System
exercises.explanation: Particle systems spawn objects, update physics, and remove dead ones. Filter arrays to efficiently remove particles.

exercises.title: Circular Progress Ring
hints: Build arcs by looping through segments
Calculate angle from start to end
Use stroke style with round cap
exercises.explanation: Progress rings are built as arcs. The foreground arc length is based on progress (0-1).

exercises.title: Data-Driven Bar Chart
hints: Use lerp formula for smooth animation
exercises.explanation: Bar charts interpolate toward target values for smooth animation. Colors generated from index create rainbow effect.

exercises.title: Fix Conflicting Winding in a Spike Burst
hints: If cross <= 0, swap base vertices before drawing
Close every contour after line segments
exercises.explanation: In multi-contour paths, mixed winding can cancel fills under the even-odd rule. Cross-product checks enforce consistent contour direction.

exercises.title: Read and Display ViewModel Data
hints: Use context:viewModel() to get the VM
Access .value to read the current value
exercises.explanation: ViewModels provide reactive properties that scripts can read. Use context:viewModel() in init.

exercises.title: Writing to ViewModel Properties
exercises.explanation: ViewModel properties are read/write. Assign to .value to update them.

exercises.title: Listening for Property Changes
hints: Update visuals based on new state
exercises.explanation: Listeners make scripts reactive to external changes. Callbacks fire automatically when properties change.

exercises.title: Firing Triggers
exercises.explanation: Triggers are one-shot events with no persistent value. Use them for notifications.

exercises.title: Nested ViewModel Inputs
exercises.explanation: Input<Data.X> binds to a specific ViewModel instance assigned in the editor.

exercises.title: Single Responsibility Principle
hints: The lerp function interpolates between two values: result = a + (b - a) * t
Use the Easing functions in advance() to animate the position
Util scripts hold pure functions, Node scripts handle visual behavior
exercises.explanation: Single Responsibility Principle keeps code maintainable. Util scripts hold pure functions with no side effects, while Node scripts handle visual behavior and state.

exercises.title: State Management Patterns
hints: Use SCALE_BY_STATE[newState] to get the target scale
Use COLOR_BY_STATE[newState] to get the color for the new state
Lookup tables make state machines maintainable
exercises.explanation: Union types and lookup tables make state machines type-safe and maintainable. The compiler catches invalid states, and configuration changes require updating only the lookup tables.

exercises.title: Layered Architecture
hints: In Particle.update: update position with velocity, apply gravity to vy, increment life
In advance: loop through particles, call Particle.update, keep alive ones
Layered architecture separates Config, Data, and Orchestration
exercises.explanation: Layered architecture separates concerns into modules: Config for constants, Data modules for pure logic, and Node scripts for orchestration. Each layer can be tested and modified independently.

exercises.title: Tracing Execution Flow
hints: Use print() with string interpolation to show the function name and relevant data
Limit prints in advance to avoid console spam
exercises.explanation: Understanding when lifecycle functions are called is essential for debugging. init runs once, update runs when inputs change, advance runs every frame.

exercises.title: Debugging State Changes
hints: Create a logState function that prints a formatted string with label and values
Call it from init and when deltaX > 1
exercises.explanation: Tracking state changes over time helps identify issues like values not updating, updating incorrectly, or oscillating unexpectedly. Helper functions ensure consistent formatting.

exercises.title: Debugging a Broken Script
hints: Bug 1: Initialize self.path before calling methods on it
exercises.explanation: Common bugs include uninitialized fields (nil errors), typos in property names, and accessing undefined fields. Strict mode catches many of these at edit time.

exercises.title: Cache and Reuse Objects
hints: Create Path and Paint objects once in init, then reuse them
Use path:reset() to clear and rebuild geometry without allocating new objects
draw() should only render, not allocate
exercises.explanation: Creating objects every frame is expensive. Allocating Path and Paint once in init and reusing them eliminates per-frame allocation overhead.

exercises.title: Update-Driven Rendering
hints: Create a rebuild helper function that resets and rebuilds the path
Call it from init for initial state, and from update when inputs change
draw() remains lightweight, only rendering the cached path
exercises.explanation: Update-driven rendering only rebuilds geometry when inputs change, not every frame. This pattern is essential for complex shapes that are expensive to rebuild.

exercises.title: Your First Working Script
hints: Make sure you created a Node Script (not Util Script)
The script must be attached to a shape on the Artboard
Press Play to run the script and see console output
Check the Console panel (View → Console) for the ANSWER line
exercises.explanation: This exercise teaches the complete workflow: creating a script, attaching it to a shape, and verifying it runs correctly via console output. The Problems panel catches errors before you run.
